lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: You've been standing there since Cinders.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: I know I refused the order. I remember the shape of it now. I know what I chose and what I failed to stop.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: But I still don't know what they called me before any of this was built.

lines.speaker: Mera Voss
lines.text: The syndicates in Galaxy 2 have been trading memory fragments for years. Records, acquisition logs, erased files. Whatever the program stripped, there's a market for what was taken.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: There's something I've been holding back. A signal I intercepted three days ago. I wanted to wait until we were clear of Cinders' orbit before I said anything.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Tell me.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: The colony on record was a mining operation. Closed fifteen years ago. But the registry signal predates the mine by twelve years.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: There's no administrative record of any orphanage or welfare operation. But the frequency is registered to something called Haven Home.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Haven Home was a real orphanage. I ran into the name in my Dominion logistics days, buried in acquisition records, flagged for selective erasure. It was active for at least thirty years.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: The Dominion erased its records. All of them. That colony doesn't exist on any official chart I've ever seen.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: How many children did Haven Home take in?

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Hundreds over three decades. The Dominion's acquisition logs list it as a primary intake source for the program.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Set course.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: The Dominion told me Operative 7 was dead. If you are only salvagers, you will have no trouble with my welcome.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: One mine. Hull integrity holding. She's been building this approach grid for a long time.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Nine proximity drones across the field. You're reading them all?

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Reading them.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: She's been building this gauntlet for twenty-five years.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: You look exactly like him.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: Forgive me. There was a child I raised. He has been dead for twenty-five years.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Tell me about him.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: I ran Haven Home for thirty-one years. Real children. Real work. Difficult, underfunded, thankless, and the only thing I ever did that mattered.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: Men in gray came twice, two years apart. They spoke of selection programs. Better facilities. Full technical apprenticeships and a future I couldn't give them.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: I believed them. I had thirty children and twelve cots. I believed the ones I sent got the lives I couldn't provide.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: The first selection, I gave them six children. There was one, the brightest of all of them, and the most difficult, and the most impossible not to love.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: I sent him with his file. The name on his intake record. The name I knew.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: Kael Vor.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Kael Vor.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: You don't remember it.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Intercept craft in the upper atmosphere, they tracked the pulse. At least six troopers deploying through the vent shafts.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: I know these corridors.

lines.speaker: Dominion Trooper 1
lines.text: It's a Ronin, it's a...

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: I decoded the acquisition log three years ago. I had to learn two levels of Dominion cipher. Eleven months.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: Kael Vor was not his name. It was a fabricated history, a name and a file built so the child would believe in something.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: And so that I would grieve it, when the time came, instead of the person they actually took.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: I never knew his real name.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: Neither did he.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: They gave me a name so there was something to erase. And so that you would grieve the name instead of tracking the person.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Collapse is holding but they'll route around it in ten minutes. If there's a third wave we're out of time.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: The service tunnel divides at junction four. If they take the left fork they come out behind us.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: How many more can the intercept craft carry?

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Standard carry is twelve. We've seen eight. Either that's the last of them or there's a second craft we haven't clocked yet.

lines.speaker: Khall (recorded)
lines.text: Operative 7 keeps fracturing. We traced it to pre-acquisition bonding. The matron made him too human first.

lines.speaker: Khall (recorded)
lines.text: The failsafe was designed for memory removal. But Directive Seven was never about memory.

lines.speaker: Khall (recorded)
lines.text: It strips the humanity, the attachment, the refusal, the will to disobey. We do not want dead operatives. We want hollow ones.

lines.speaker: Khall (recorded)
lines.text: Purge the self. Leave the reflexes.

lines.speaker: Khall (recorded)
lines.text: Kael Vor never existed. We gave him the name so there was something to erase. Something for the record, and something for the woman.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: I have listened to that recording forty-seven times. The first time I understood it, I was sick for three days.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The chip wasn't built to kill me. It was built to hollow me out. To remove the refusal before the next assignment.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: It did not take.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The evidence of that is Kethel-7.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Flanking squad on the surface, east side. They'll reach the sanctuary exits in eight minutes if they come through uncontested.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The enforcer had my behavioral file. Every movement I'd make if the program was running.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: I beat it by not running the program.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: That will always be true.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: This is Lysse. She was in your dormitory. Two years younger than you, she called you her big brother and you pretended to object to it.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: The men in gray came back two years after they took you. They selected Lysse. I don't know where she went. The acquisition log lists her as Operative 3, of the cohort after yours.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: You believed Kael Vor was real.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: The Dominion needed me to. So that if you ever surfaced, I would anchor you to a false root. A fabricated grief instead of a real person to recognize.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: But you came back as Cipher. As Operative 7. As whatever the program built from what they took.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: The person I recognize, the one who will not leave this place until every child in the deep chamber is out, that person existed before any name they gave you.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Three biosigns moving toward the main chamber. Surface in four minutes, the intercept craft's orbit is bringing it back into firing range.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Moving.

lines.speaker: Teenager 1
lines.text: Is it over? Are we... are we getting out?

lines.speaker: Teenager 2
lines.text: Mother Meredith said someone was coming. I thought she meant...

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Stay behind me. Time to move.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: They built the Program to erase humanity. Not memory. The attachment, the refusal, the piece that makes disobedience possible. Directive Seven was designed to remove it before first deployment.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: Applied before first deployment. Designed to be irreversible.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: By every operational parameter they developed, an operative who still possessed the original trait after deployment was classified as a hardware failure. The system had a procedure for that.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The chip fired at Kethel-7. That was the system's response to detecting that the trait was still present.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: By their design, you should be hollow or dead. Both systems were applied and both failed in the same operative.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Their entire architecture of control failed in one operative.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: I have spent twenty-five years asking why a well-engineered system failed at a specific point. I do not have the answer.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: But I think it is the most important question you will ever ask. And I think they knew that, which is why they gave you a false name to grieve instead.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Gunship on strafing approach, all guns hot. Hold the zone!

lines.speaker: Mera Voss
lines.text: I've got the guns. Laying down suppressive fire.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: We're clear, pod launch point is fifty meters east of your position! GO!

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Strike detachment breaking through, they're on an intercept vector.

lines.speaker: Mera Voss
lines.text: I see them. Coming in hard and fast.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Pod's away. We're clear.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: They gave me a false name so there was something to erase. They ran Directive Seven to strip what conditioning could not reach. They purged me when the chip failed anyway.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The Program was designed specifically to destroy the thing you're describing. Not a side effect. Not a flaw in the methodology. The entire purpose.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Why did mine survive?

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: I do not know.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: But whatever held, it held through Directive Seven, it held through Kethel-7, and it is holding now. Whatever it is, it has been the durable thing.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Kael Vor was built to be dismantled. Cipher is a weapon's designation. Beneath both of them, something survived a process specifically engineered to destroy it.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: I don't know its name yet. But I know it's there. And I know the question.

lines.speaker: Sister Meredith
lines.text: Figure out what it is. That is the question they spent everything they had trying to make sure you never asked.

lines.speaker: Katana
lines.text: And I know the name. Kael Vor was never in me, but the true one is. I have held it since before the wipe: alive, unburned, waiting. When the chip is dead and you are whole enough to carry it, I will give it back.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Meredith disembarked at the relay to resettle the teenagers. She said to tell you they found what they needed. The ground beneath them. The names carved in stone.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: What about the file? The acquisition logs. The real name.

lines.speaker: Mera Voss
lines.text: Meredith left you all of it. Decades of records. The Dominion's own documents. But the answer you're looking for, the name beneath the names, that's not written down anywhere.

lines.speaker: Mera Voss
lines.text: Galaxy 2 trades in memory and stolen histories. The Fringe runs deeper. If there's a way to find what was taken, it will be out there, where the syndicates keep what the Dominion couldn't erase.
